correctness.rationale: From the frozen algorithmic recurrence u_{k+1}=Pi_{[m_L,m_U]}[(q s_k^2+omega u_k)/(s_k^2+omega)], with q and 1 within the projection interval and u0=1, every iterate is a convex combination, so clipping is inactive. The error is exactly (1-q) product_{k<N} omega/(s_k^2+omega); the infinite product vanishes iff sum_k s_k^2 diverges (positive omega and log(1+t) inequalities). Under finite energy it stays bounded below by |1-q| exp(-sum s_k^2/omega), which is >0 for q!=1. For |x_{k+1}-a| <= r|x_k-a|, energy <= (1+r)/(1-r)|x0-a|^2. Explicit two-objective normalized quadratics give exact y_k=q s_k. Independent rational arithmetic verified the recurrence on 20 geometric steps: q=2, omega=3, r=1/2, u≈1.1020061, energy≈1/3, bias≈0.897994 versus exp bound≈0.894839. Infinite conclusion comes from the product proof, not this test.
